intuition.title: Precursor and drying branches
intuition.text: Sol–gel hydrolysis of zirconium n-propoxide and precipitation from zirconium oxychloride are distinct recipes. Each has oven (110 °C, 12 h) and Rotavapor vacuum (70 °C, 50 mbar, duration unreported) drying branches, followed by 400, 500, 600 or 700 °C calcination for 4 h in static air. The four uncalcined states remain separate supporting specimens.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Sections 2.1–2.3 and Scheme 1

intuition.title: Sol–gel feed ambiguity is retained
intuition.text: The paper describes purchased 70 wt% zirconium propoxide solution, dilution to 30 wt%, a 0.025 M precursor and a typical charge of 17.7 g Zr-P plus 41.3 g n-propanol. Whether the stated precursor mass denotes stock solution or neat-equivalent reagent is unresolved. No molar charge or corrected concentration is inferred.

intuition.title: Phase fractions and domain sizes are separate
intuition.text: Table 1 reports XRD peak-area tetragonal/monoclinic fractions; blank cells and the printed dash do not become inferred zeros. Table 2 gives phase/reflection-specific Scherrer crystallite sizes and lattice strains, not SEM particle diameters. Its strain unit or scale is unspecified. At 700 °C, SG-O is 23 nm in Table 2 but 20 nm in the prose; both are retained with the explicit table used in structured measurements.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3,5–6, Tables 1–2 and structural discussion

intuition.title: Stabilization is an interpretation
intuition.text: The authors relate retention of tetragonal zirconia to small crystallites, hydroxyl groups and lattice strain, with greater thermal stability for sol–gel material. Vacuum drying initially produces larger domains. These explanations and the cited critical-size literature are not additional measured thresholds or current sample recipes. Exact residual tetragonal fractions at high temperature are retained instead of treating summarized complete transformation as zero.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4,6–7, Structural discussion and conclusions

intuition.title: Before-calcination morphology has its own scope
intuition.text: Figure 6 shows spherical sol–gel particles after either drying route. Precipitation gives predominantly cubic/rectangular particles of varying sizes after oven drying, with some spherical particles after vacuum drying. These images are before calcination; no numerical SEM particle mean or automatic post-calcination shape is assigned.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 6–7, Figure 6 and Section 3.4

intuition.title: Textural and thermal measurements
intuition.text: Table 3 reports only before-calcination and 400 °C textural values. Surface areas and pore volumes decrease while average pore diameters increase. Figure 5 shows before-calcination N2 isotherms, interpreted as combined H2/H3 hysteresis with ink-bottle and slit pores. TG/DTG weight loss of 22–33% and mechanisms remain study-level context without exact batch-specific values.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 4–7, Thermal discussion, Figure 5, Table 3 and Sections 3.2–3.3

general_background.title: Thermodynamics and kinetics
general_background.summary: Thermodynamics describes which states are energetically favoured, while kinetics governs how quickly a system can move between them. A change can be favourable yet proceed slowly when an activation barrier or limited transport restricts the pathway.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
